headline: The Commerce Department reportedly received a classified warning about Jensen Huang's affair before it broke, as forecasters updated timelines toward a 2027 intelligence explosion and experts named nuclear risk and the US-China spy game among AI's real dangers.

points.text: Axios reported that Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick received a highly classified national-security memo warning about Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's relationship with suspected Chinese spy Alice Huang.
The AI Futures Project updated its timelines, saying an intelligence explosion now looks likely to happen in 2027.
Wired asked ten experts what AI's real nightmares are, concluding that nuclear catastrophe and the fallout of the US-China 'domination game' are genuine risks, more than a Skynet-style takeover.
ControlAI laid out its doctrine for preventing AI from reaching 'points of no return.'
Wired found security flaws across multiple UK government websites that exposed 'god-tier' private information.
The AI Safety Newsletter reported that the US midterms favored candidates backing AI regulation.
The ITU's AI for Good series explored building context, control, and confidence into AI used in public and humanitarian settings.
